synopsis: Nissan is among the manufacturers whose NHTSA investigations document unnecessary automatic braking as an on-road hazard; the booklet dates the Nissan investigation to 2019 [f11168, f15428, f11173]. Nissan released a software update for the Rogue unnecessary-braking problem in early 2019 and treated it as a service action, a treatment criticized by the Center for Auto Safety [f1492]. The booklet concludes that Nissan and Tesla records show field behavior changing materially after software or firmware updates [f2013]. These investigations, alongside NHTSA testing and mining research, underpin the recommendation to test large sets of situations that appear dangerous but should not trigger braking [f1992]. The status of the Nissan investigation remains uncertain in the booklet [f1963].

relations.note: Both identify NHTSA investigations as documentation of unnecessary braking; the glossary also includes Daimler trucks.
Dates the Nissan false-braking investigation to 2019.
Provides the year for Nissan's contribution to the glossary's investigation record.
Documented false-braking hazards support testing situations where braking should not activate.
Nissan's corrective software release supports the relevance of software changes to field behavior.
Investigation occurrence is established, but its status remains uncertain.
